# Relay

> Relay is a Zimbabwean errand and delivery marketplace. It connects customers
> with independent runners who collect, buy and deliver things — within
> Zimbabwe and along the Zimbabwe–South Africa corridor. Relay never holds
> anyone's money: the customer pays the runner directly, and Relay charges only
> a small fee for the introduction. Every job leaves a permanent, timestamped
> record that either side can use if something goes wrong.

Relay is in closed beta and operates primarily in Harare, with cross-border
runs to and from South Africa.

## What Relay is and is not

Relay is a directory and a record-keeper. It introduces two people who want an
errand done, records what they agree between themselves, and keeps the evidence
in case they later disagree.

Relay does **not**: hold money, set prices, decide what a runner is paid,
assign work to anybody, carry anything itself, employ runners, or guarantee
that a job will be done. Customers declare what they will pay and pay the
runner directly. Runners choose which jobs to accept.

Relay is not a bank, a payment processor, an escrow service, a courier company,
or a ride-hailing platform.

## How it works

1. A customer posts an errand — what they need, where it goes, when it is
   needed, what they will pay, and how they will pay it.
2. Runners nearby see it and choose whether to accept. Nothing is assigned.
3. Both parties have their identity checked before they can take work.
4. At the door, both open a screen showing the same code, so each can confirm
   the other is who they say they are.
5. Photographs are taken at collection and handover, so the condition of
   anything is on record.
6. The customer pays the runner directly, and confirms in the app.

## Common questions

**What is Relay?** A Zimbabwean marketplace for errands and deliveries,
connecting customers with identity-verified independent runners.

**How do I send a parcel in Harare?** Post what you need on Relay, say where
it is going and what you will pay, and a runner nearby can accept it.

**How do I send something between Zimbabwe and South Africa?** Relay supports
the corridor. Carriage across the border is licensed work; runners state which
courier licence they hold and customers can see it.

**Does Relay hold my money?** No. You pay your runner directly, in cash or by
whichever mobile wallet you both agree — EcoCash, InnBucks, OneMoney, O'Mari,
Mukuru or a bank transfer. Relay never touches it.

**What does Relay cost?** A small fixed fee that depends on what the job is
worth, charged to the customer and never deducted from what the runner is paid.
It is free during the closed beta.

**Is it safe?** Every runner's identity is checked against a government
document before they can accept work. Both parties confirm each other with a
shared code at the door, photographs record what changed hands, and every job
keeps a permanent record that can be given to the police if something serious
happens.

**Who runs Relay?** It is built and operated in Zimbabwe.

- [Download](https://relay.africa/download): the Android app, installed
  directly.
- [Terms of Service](https://relay.africa/legal): the agreement, including

- [Data & Cookie Policy](https://relay.africa/data-policy.html): what this
  website and the app store on your device.
